chapter: Erroll Garner and the Los Angeles scene
title: Art Tatum after hours at Lovejoy's
summary: Everyone went to hear Tatum after work.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: That's the time when he had the trio with Doc West and Red Callender, I guess.
Yeah, this is when they were working at the Suzy Q.
Then like you said, you couldn't play together or even hear each other, because you were working on the same schedule.
But how about the after-hours scene out there? It was supposed to be a pretty heavy scene in L.A. at that time.
Well, at that time Art Tatum was out there. So after everybody got off work, you knew that's where they was heading, to go over to hear him.

Yeah, at Lovejoy's, to see if he was on that night. Because some nights, he was amazing! We'd go by there and, man, we'd come back with our mouth wide open, going "What the hell happened?" It was out of sight.
Did Erroll and Art ever play??

Yeah, he would sit in... After Tatum would get up and walk away from the piano, Erroll might go in and sit down and play a number or two. But he never did stretch out where Art Tatum was playing. I would have liked to hear that. In fact, I tried to egg it on a couple of times, but it didn't happen. Just Erroll played his little thing, you know, and Art Tatum came back and roared through the piano.
